llm.summary: This skill is a local note-and-file organizer that stores user-provided content in the browser and does not show network upload or hidden execution behavior.

dimensions.detail: Browser localStorage, IndexedDB, clipboard access, file upload, and download behavior are disclosed and proportionate to a local clipboard/note/archive tool.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill delivers a static HTML file and optionally describes packaging the directory with an external skill-creator script; no bundled installer or executable persistence was found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The activation text is somewhat broad, especially the mention of packaging HTML as an installable skill, but the artifact otherwise scopes behavior to this app and local document workflows.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Persistence is limited to browser localStorage and IndexedDB keys for notes, trash, drafts, folders, images, and uploaded file blobs; no background worker, credential use, privilege escalation, or network exfiltration was found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is a single-file frontend app for collecting text, managing pasted images/files, organizing folders, and exporting Word documents; the inspected HTML implements those features coherently.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you want a local browser-based text, image, and document organizer. Content you paste or upload can remain stored in your browser until cleared, so avoid using it on shared browser profiles unless you are comfortable with that local persistence.
llm.findings: [SQP-1] expected: The scanner's concern about broad activation is partially supported by the description, but this is an invocation-quality issue rather than evidence of hidden or unsafe runtime behavior; users should treat the HTML-packaging phrase narrowly.
